prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: full-fidelity visual-direction comp for a native iOS rail app
Primary request: Design the category-standard version of a complete portrait iPhone first-screen UI for Last Train, an after-dark one-handed rail departure app.
Scene/backdrop: full-bleed 393x852-style app screen only, no phone hardware frame, no marketing poster.
Exact visible content: "LAST TRAIN", "FAST TRAIN", "Upminster", "EAST", "23:47", "Shoeburyness", "22:58", "23:18", "23:32", "FIRST BACK", "05:12", "Direct services only".
Information hierarchy: station and direction scope; a clearly dominant final direct train at 23:47; three earlier departure rows; first train back. No journey durations. No +1 or calendar-next-day labels.
Visual world: the premium contemporary transit-app category standard, executed impeccably. Native iOS dark appearance with SF Pro typography, restrained blue tint, high-quality frosted glass panels, subtle system materials and elevation, familiar segmented mode and direction controls, large tabular departure numerals, clean spacing, and excellent legibility. Use #FF304C only for the final last-train state; never for errors or decoration.
Composition: conventional navigation title, polished station selector, East/West control, and stacked departure cards. No bottom tab bar because there are only two modes. Respect the Dynamic Island safe area and 44pt touch targets.
Constraints: must look like a shipped native iOS app, not a web dashboard or concept poster; exact rail content should be readable; no ticket purchase, maps, journey duration, advertising, invented claims, or watermark.
